explanation: A single foreign key in either parent table cannot represent a many-to-many relationship. The proper fix is an associative table that stores one row per pairing and references both sides.

options.text: Move the linkage into a separate case_doctor table with one row per doctor-case pair
Add more doctor_id columns to the case table, one for each possible doctor
Store a single case_id inside the doctor table instead
Remove both identifiers and infer the relationship from names

prompt: A clinic wants to track which doctors work on which cases. A doctor can work on many cases, and a case can involve many doctors. Which schema change best fixes a design that currently stores only doctor_id inside the case table?

source.section: Creating a relational database with an m:m relationship
